channel.title: The Rambam's Eight Chapters — Dayan Daniel Kada
channel.description: Dayan Daniel Kada's series on the Rambam's Eight Chapters: the soul, character, the middle path, free will and repentance.

item.title: One Soul, Five Powers: Know Yourself Before You Heal | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 1
item.description:
Knowing yourself comes before healing the soul. The opening of the Eight Chapters: why the Rambam wrote this introduction to Avot, why he left out names, and the one soul with five faculties, from nutrition and the senses to imagination, the emotions and the intellect.

item.title: Healing a Bad Trait by Going to the Other Extreme | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 4, Part 1
item.description:
How do you heal a bad trait? Chapter 4 of the Eight Chapters places good traits in the middle, warns against praising the extremes, and prescribes going to the opposite extreme for a time before returning to the middle, ideally with a mentor or friend.

item.title: Who Is a Hasid, and Is Self-Denial Holy? | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 4, Part 2
item.description:
Is it easier to cure excess or deficiency? The Rambam's hasid leans slightly to the side easier to correct, the fasting of the pious was temporary medicine, the Torah's path is moderation within society, and the Nazir brings an offering for denying himself what God permitted.

item.title: Is Your Solution Becoming the Problem? | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 4, Part 3
item.description:
When does the cure become the problem? Finishing Chapter 4: why truth and peace outrank fasts, why extra prohibitions are an extreme of their own, weighing our traits daily, Moshe's moment of anger, and managing polarities by holding both poles and moving between them.

item.title: Can Eating and Sleeping Be Serving God? | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 5
item.description:
Can eating, drinking and sleeping be service of God? Chapter 5 of the Eight Chapters sets one goal for every action, knowing God, and shows how health, pleasure as medicine and beauty serve it, so the same meal or job can be mundane or holy.

item.title: Should You Still Want What the Torah Forbids? | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 6
item.description:
Is it greater to have no desire for wrong, or to want it and resist? The Rambam reconciles the philosophers with Hazal: for rational misvot lose the desire, for hukkim it is fine to want and hold back because HaShem commanded. Chapter 7 then opens on the prophet's veils.

item.title: What Stands Between a Prophet and God? | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 7
item.description:
Every intellectual and moral flaw is a veil between a person and God. Chapter 7 of the Eight Chapters explains what a prophet needs, why anger and sadness block prophecy, how Moshe differed from everyone else, and why prophecy ceased with the Temple.

item.title: Born This Way? The Rambam Against Determinism | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 8, Part 1
item.description:
Are we born with our virtues and vices? The opening of Chapter 8 of the Eight Chapters: the Rambam rejects personal and theological determinism, explains that divine decrees concern nature and not free choices, and shows how miracles were built into creation.

item.title: Why Was Pharaoh Punished If God Hardened His Heart? | The Rambam's Eight Chapters, Chapter 8, Part 2
item.description:
Can a person lose the freedom to repent? For the Rambam the hardening was itself the punishment for earlier free choices, closing the way to teshuvah. Also: habits becoming identity, why each Egyptian chose to oppress Israel, and the views of the Ramban and Ibn Ezra.
